truths.truth: Concurrent appendRead processes at the bound lose no record across the pair and leave no held claim or private stamp that would stop a later rotation.
truths.evidence: Spot-check spawning 6 real child processes through appendRead against a root padded to 8388607 B, all started before any finished, repeated 4 times: every writer returned {"written":true}; zero tags missing across live+sibling on every run; planning root held exactly reads.jsonl, reads.1.jsonl, reads.1.jsonl.claim - no *.rotate.*, *.evict.* or *.claim.<pid> stamp; live and sibling distinct inodes; a subsequent pad-to-bound append still rotated and landed ({"written":true}, live 134 B), proving the inert shared .claim sidecar left by a completed rotation blocks nothing. Losers' private stamps are dropped by the `if (pending) unlinkSync(pending)` arm of rotateReads' finally. Test row 'writers racing at the bound leave ONE generation, no claim and no record lost' passes.

truths.truth: An abandoned claim is reclaimed on the next append rather than disabling rotation forever, and an unknowable claim age fails live.
truths.evidence: readsClaimAbandoned uses statSync(claim).mtimeMs against READS_CLAIM_STALE_MS = 30_000 and returns false on any throw. Spot-check building the killed-claim state directly (record at 8388607 B, sibling linkSync'd to it, sidecar utimes'd): sidecar 120 s old -> {"written":true} in 1 ms, live 139 B starting with the rotation marker, sibling a distinct inode holding 8388607 B. Sidecar dated now -> claim left standing, 255 ms wait, append still lands (live 8388664 B), sibling still the same inode. No sidecar at all -> identical (255 ms, claim held, {"written":true}). Test rows 'an ABANDONED claim is reclaimed rather than disabling rotation forever', 'a LIVE claim is left standing, at the cost of one deferred rotation', 'a claim carrying NO sidecar at all reads as live, the same way' and 'a COMPLETED rotation leaves its sidecar behind, inert, and does not rotate again' all pass.

truths.truth: No residue this phase's own rotation writes into .planning/ is left for the next `git add .planning` to sweep in.
truths.evidence: rotateReads writes two private paths inside the planning root that no ignore rule covers: `${file}.rotate.${pid}.${rand}` (cadence-core/bin/lib/read-trace.mjs:669, the fresh marker record) and `${sibling}.evict.${pid}.${rand}` (:637, a WHOLE prior generation, up to 8 MiB). READS_IGNORE_LINES (cadence-core/bin/planning/trace.mjs:109-114) covers only reads.jsonl, reads.1.jsonl, reads.1.jsonl.claim and reads.1.jsonl.claim.*, and this repo's .gitignore:39-42 is the same four. Verified: `git check-ignore -v .planning/reads.jsonl.rotate.9.x .planning/reads.1.jsonl.evict.9.x` exits 1 (no match) both in this repository and in a fresh repo where `trace ignore` had just run. The finally block unlinks both on every ordinary arm, so this only strands on process death - but the hook runs under a 5 s timeout (hooks/hooks.json:15-25) and a kill inside the rotation window leaves an unignored file of up to MAX_READS_BYTES, which is exactly the sweep D-11 exists to prevent. CONTEXT defers the TRACE's .rotate/.evict temps explicitly and calls them 'the trace's residue'; the reads-side pair is residue this phase itself introduced and no line defers it.
